plan.summary: Budget concentrates on Ruffco, the one large pet-retail checkout where new-kitten owners actually appear, with Pawline as a subscription-comfort test; Tailcrate is out as a direct pet-subscription competitor and everything non-pet lacks any purchase-moment link.

recommended.name: Ruffco
recommended.tier_reason: The computed tier capped Ruffco at test over an 'adjacent conflict' on pet_supplies, but this publisher sells food, supplies and pharmacy items, not a curated new-kitten subscription with a what-to-expect booklet, so it isn't a substitute a shopper would buy instead. The purchase moment is exact: someone stocking up at the largest pet retailer in the catalog is a pet owner, and the new-kitten cohort inside 62M impressions is large enough to read quickly at a $40 offer against a $73 basket.
recommended.rationale: A shopper checking out of a broad pet retailer ('pet_food', 'pet_supplies', 'pet_pharmacy') is already provisioning an animal, and the new-kitten slice of the 'Largest pet audience in the catalog' is the single best-defined moment for a first-three-months box; $40 sits comfortably under the $73 typical basket.

evidence.quote: Largest pet audience in the catalog

recommended.risk: Most of this traffic is existing owners and likely dog-skewed; only a small share are days-old kitten adopters, so creative must qualify hard on 'just got a kitten' or CPA will drift.

test.name: Pawline
test.rationale: Subscription-heavy pet buyers are already comfortable with recurring pet billing, which suits a subscription-only box, but the same shopper may have just started a kitten food subscription here, so this is worth measuring rather than funding.

evidence.quote: Subscription-heavy. Owners are health-conscious about pets, responsive to premium positioning

test.risk: Audience is 'responsive to premium positioning' and health-focused; a playful toy-and-samples box may read as low-value, and 4.8M impressions make a clean read slow.

bid_strategy.rationale: $40 first order (assumed) × 0.60 = $24.00 target CPA: subscription revenue repeats, so a first order can be bought at a larger share of its value. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

test_plan.hypothesis: Subscription-heavy pet buyers are already comfortable with recurring pet billing, which suits a subscription-only box, but the same shopper may have just started a kitten food subscription here, so this is worth measuring rather than funding.
test_plan.risk: Audience is 'responsive to premium positioning' and health-focused; a playful toy-and-samples box may read as low-value, and 4.8M impressions make a clean read slow.
test_plan.promote_if: CPA at or below the $24.00 target after 14 days: move it to core.
test_plan.cut_if: CPA above the $31.20 maximum, or no conversions after 14 days: stop it.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

launch_summary.summary: $8,500 of the $10,000 budget goes to Ruffco, the one large pet-retail checkout where new-kitten owners actually show up, running all four persona ads from The Pet Parent to The Value-Conscious Shopper. The remaining $1,500 tests Pawline, to learn whether subscription-comfortable pet buyers respond to a playful toy-and-samples box or read it as low-value. Pawline moves to core if cost per new customer lands at or below $24.00 after 14 days, and stops if it exceeds $31.20. Tailcrate was excluded as a direct pet-subscription competitor.
uncertainties: The $40 first order value is assumed, and the $24.00 target cost per new customer is built on it, so a lower real price makes the whole bid too generous.
The review flags doubt about whether this is a consumer or business offering, which would change who the ads are written for.
Pawline's audience leans premium and health-focused with 4.8M impressions, so a clean read within 14 days may not arrive.
questions: What does the first box actually cost the customer?
What is the margin and expected lifetime value of a subscriber, so the target can replace the 60%-of-first-order rule?
Is the box sold as a recurring three-month subscription, or also as a one-off gift kit?
